section.title: Passion needs an operating model that survives your absence
section.deck: Peterman recounts the transition from a six-month personal experiment to a self-sustaining podcast.

blocks.text: Peterman began the podcast while employed at Meta, partly to practice speaking and share career stories he found inspiring. The work kept drawing his attention after hours, but he says it had only lost money. A reorganization provided an opportunity to leave and test the idea using six months of savings. He describes a personal decision driven by the work he wanted to do, rather than a financially obvious career move.
blocks.heading: A bounded experiment outside the obvious career path

blocks.text: The early freedom came with an operational weakness: he personally researched guests, reviewed all the footage, and handled the production. Despite working more than before, he struggled to maintain one episode per week. If he stopped, the production stopped. Four months into the intended runway, he still had no revenue and had postponed finding sponsors because that effort competed with the parts of creating he enjoyed.
blocks.heading: The founder was the bottleneck

blocks.text: Illness made the fragility concrete. A nearly finished episode allowed him to publish during a week when he could not work, but the experience pushed him to take sponsors seriously and build a backlog. He made recording more efficient so he could produce two episodes a week when needed. He also reduced spending by filming episodes himself, including an interview in a guest’s study with two phones. Sponsorships then brought in revenue.
blocks.heading: Create room for interruptions

blocks.text: By the update, the six-month experiment had lasted nine months and he said the podcast was sustaining itself. His keyboard project had also raised its required Kickstarter funds quickly. He did not treat these facts as proof that leaving Meta maximized income: he expected the keyboard project could lose money in aggregate and emphasized that money was not its main goal.
blocks.heading: Sustainability and income maximization are different goals

blocks.text: His condition for continuing was practical: the podcast needed to cover itself and his living costs. He wanted to improve guest access and produce the keyboard at a high quality bar. He had been using an early manufacturing sample and described shipping as a future target. The captions do not provide the publication date needed to convert “early next year” into a reliable calendar deadline, and this account does not establish current shipping status.
